title: NVIDIA Research releases open Déjà View (DVLT) 3D reconstruction model
summary: NVIDIA Research, ETH Zurich, and the University of Toronto have released Déjà View (DVLT), an open-source recurrent transformer for feed-forward multi-view 3D reconstruction. Using a 117-million parameter weight-tied architecture with a tunable inference-time refinement step count K, the model predicts per-pixel depth, confidence, ray maps, and camera poses with code and weights available on GitHub and Hugging Face.
research_notes:
Clone the official repository from https://github.com/nv-tlabs/dvlt and install the required PyTorch and DINOv2 environment dependencies.

Download the pre-trained 117M model checkpoint from the Hugging Face repository nvidia/dvlt.

Run the multi-view inference script on an unposed set of RGB images or video frames, choosing the recurrent iteration step count K based on available compute budget.

Extract predicted per-pixel depth maps, confidence masks, camera intrinsics/extrinsics, and ray-derived 3D point clouds for downstream 3D Gaussian splatting or mesh reconstruction.

Configure the recurrent step count K between 8 and 16 at inference time to trade off reconstruction precision against latency without loading different checkpoints.

Filter low-confidence depth predictions using the predicted per-pixel confidence masks prior to multi-view geometric fusion.

Ensure input RGB sets maintain adequate visual overlap across views to optimize geometric consistency across recurrent transformer passes.
